title: Persist verified Git repository transfer procedure for sandbox work
objective: Preserve in the MCF source of truth the verified procedure for moving an exact Git repository snapshot into the ChatGPT sandbox when direct sandbox egress is unavailable, so future missions can reuse the proven path instead of rediscovering failed alternatives.
expected_outcome: A durable, auditable MCF knowledge record containing the successful transfer pattern, failed alternatives, integrity checks, evidence references and an explicit efficiency rule for future repository-review missions.
scope: GitHub Actions artifact bridge for repository transfer
full .git preservation when a real clone is required
git rev-parse and git fsck validation
reuse of the MCF repository as a transport bridge for repositories without workflows
out_of_scope: exposure or extraction of credentials or secrets
mutation of the Cognitive Ledger repository
retesting known failed transfer paths unless the execution environment materially changes
authorizations: Persist this mission descriptor in a dedicated MCF branch and PR
Record non-secret operational evidence from the completed transfer experiments
prohibitions: Do not copy tokens, cookies, passwords or environment secret values into mission artifacts
Do not bypass MCF merge or release gates
Do not treat a worktree archive without .git as a full clone when Git history is required

preferred_method.name: GitHub Actions artifact bridge
procedure: Resolve the target repository and exact canonical commit SHA from GitHub.

Use an existing workflow_dispatch-capable repository as a temporary transport bridge; when the target repository has no suitable workflow, the MCF repository can act as the bridge without modifying the target repository.
Create a temporary branch only in the bridge repository.
Make the workflow checkout the target repository at the exact requested SHA with full history when a real clone is required.
Run git integrity checks before packaging.
Package the worktree together with .git, write an internal SHA-256 manifest and publish the package with actions/upload-artifact.
Download the GitHub Actions artifact through the authorized GitHub connector so it materializes under /mnt/data in the sandbox.
Validate artifact contents for unsafe archive paths before extraction.
Validate the internal SHA-256 manifest after download.
Extract the repository, normalize ownership if the runner UID causes Git safe-directory protection, then verify git rev-parse HEAD, branch/tracking state, git status and git fsck.
Delete the temporary transport branch locally and remotely after successful verification.
preferred_method.efficiency_rule: Start with this method for future exact repository-to-sandbox transfers. Do not repeat previously failed alternatives unless tooling, network policy or connector capabilities have materially changed.

validated_examples.notes: Full Git history and .git were transferred; final sandbox clone was clean on main tracking origin/main and passed git fsck.

The target repository had no .github/workflows on main, so MCF was used only as a transport bridge. Cognitive Ledger itself remained unmodified. The transferred main contained only README.md at that SHA; newer implementation work existed on feature branches.

known_failed_or_inferior_paths.method: Direct git clone or curl from the sandbox
known_failed_or_inferior_paths.reason: Sandbox outbound network egress to GitHub was blocked; DNS overrides did not solve the underlying egress restriction.

known_failed_or_inferior_paths.method: Managed direct download of GitHub repository archive
known_failed_or_inferior_paths.reason: The managed downloader/browser path could not materialize the GitHub binary archive endpoint for this session.

known_failed_or_inferior_paths.method: Existing workflow artifacts from unrelated CI runs
known_failed_or_inferior_paths.reason: Available artifacts contained test/evidence outputs rather than a complete repository checkout.

known_failed_or_inferior_paths.method: Direct binary read through Remote Desktop Commander
known_failed_or_inferior_paths.reason: Binary tar.gz files were not exposed as transferable file bytes by the text-oriented read path.

known_failed_or_inferior_paths.method: Base64 relay through Desktop Commander output
known_failed_or_inferior_paths.reason: A small block passed end-to-end SHA-256 verification, but scaling it to megabytes would be inefficient and consume connector quota.
No configured CLI bridge was present on the authorized Linux host during the experiment.

integrity_requirements: Bind the transfer to an explicit source repository and exact commit SHA.
Preserve .git when the task requires history, branch state or git fsck rather than static source inspection only.
Verify the package SHA-256 after download.
Reject unsafe archive paths before extraction.
Verify git rev-parse HEAD equals the expected SHA after extraction.
Verify git status is clean and branch/tracking state is intentional.
Run git fsck before claiming the transferred clone is healthy.
Remove temporary transport branches after successful verification.

acceptance_criteria: The mission descriptor is versioned in the MCF repository on a dedicated branch and reviewed through a PR.
The successful transfer method is documented with exact integrity checks and cleanup requirements.
The MCF and Cognitive Ledger transfer examples retain their canonical SHA provenance.
Known failed or inferior paths are documented to prevent unnecessary repetition.
No credential or secret value is persisted in the knowledge record.
Future MCF missions can identify the preferred transfer path without reconstructing this experiment from chat history.
next_action: Miriam consolidates this mission knowledge into the canonical MCF continuity/memory documentation; Augusto verifies provenance and traceability; Mestre prepares the result for human review before any merge.
